sentences.text:
Hon'Ble Smt. Justice G. Anupama Chakravarthy
 Criminial Petition No.5373 of 2023

This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 482 of Code of Criminal Procedure (for short 'Cr.P.C.')
by the petitioner/accused to quash the proceedings in FIR No.3 of 2023 on the file of Station House Officer, Central Crime Station, Hyderabad, registered for the offences under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC').
2.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri S.Ganesh, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for respondent - State.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is innocent and a false case has been foisted against him by respondent No.2.
Therefore, prayed to quash the FIR.

4. On the other hand, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor contended that there are five criminal cases registered against the petitioner and this Court in one of the quash petition filed by the petitioner herein has directed the petitioner to appear before the investigating officer.
In spite of the said direction, the petitioner is not co-operating with the investigating officer.
Therefore, it is not a fit case to be quashed.

5. Taking into consideration that all the offences alleged against the petitioner are punishable less than seven (07) years, this Court deems it appropriate to direct the petitioner/accused to appear before the investigating officer on 26.06.2023 between 02:00 p.m. and 04:00 p.m. and the investigating officer is directed to follow the procedure laid down under Section 41-A Cr.P.C and also the guidelines formulated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar1 scrupulously.

6. Accordingly, the Criminal Petition is disposed of.
Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.
